content_sections.title: 1. Two vowels (8 min)
content_sections.body_text: Live has /ɪ/. Leave has /iː/. For /ɪ/, relax your tongue. For /iː/, move it higher and forward; the sound is often longer too. Say live–leave five times. Change the mouth shape and the length, not only the length.

content_sections.title: 2. Clear repair (8 min)
content_sections.body_text: B: ‘I live here.’ A: ‘Did you say leave?’ B: ‘No, live—/lɪv/.’ A: ‘Oh, you live here.’ Read both roles. Cover the lines and say them again. The question is clear, and B repeats the word that A heard wrongly.

content_sections.title: 3. Independent check (10 min)
content_sections.body_text: Your own replay is practice, not proof. For listening, ask a helper or a random text-to-speech tool to say a hidden order of live and leave; write L or E, then reveal the key. For speaking, say one word without showing it and ask the helper or tool what it heard. If no independent check is available, mark ‘not checked.’

content_sections.title: 4. Take turns (9 min)
content_sections.body_text: Make a four-line talk like the model: give one safe fact, hear one word wrongly, ask ‘Did you say …?’, then correct it. Speak both roles with a pause for each reply. Success: the reply answers the question, the correction uses live or leave clearly, and an independent listener identifies the word. Otherwise, keep it as practice only.
